paragraphs.text: That is, to humble. It was the beginning of a song by which tune this psalm was sung.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: Though many cry in their sorrows, yet they cry not earnestly to God for remedy as he did whom he confessed to be the author of his salvation.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: For he who is dead is free from all cares and business of this life and thus he says because he was unprofitable for all matters concerning man's life, and as it were cut off from this world.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: That is, from your providence and care, which is meant according to the judgment of the flesh.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: The storms of your wrath have overwhelmed me.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: He attributes the loss and displeasure of his friends to God's providence by which he partly punishes and partly tries his.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: I see no end to my sorrows.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: My eyes and face declare my sorrows.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: He shows that the time is more convenient for God to help when men call to him in their dangers, than to tarry till they are dead, and then raise them up again.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: That is, in the grave, where only the body lies without all sense and remembrance.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: I am always in great dangers and sorrows as though my life would utterly be cut off every moment.
paragraphs.label: l
